methods.name: social network analysis
methods.description: The research method that is mainly explored in sociology and communication science and focuses on the analysis of the relations between individuals and among organisations and states.

methods.name: social sequence analysis
methods.description: A computational social-science method for analysing ordered sequences of social events or states. This is a possible research method, not a universal requirement for every sociology learner or role.

methods.name: topic modelling and computational text analysis
methods.description: Methods for finding and interpreting patterns in collections of text. These can support social research when the question and data justify them; they are optional methods rather than requirements for every role.

methods.name: computational models of social dynamics
methods.description: Mathematical or computational models used to explore social processes and develop or test theory. This is a research specialization, not a general employment requirement.

methods.name: analysis of online and computer-mediated social behaviour
methods.description: Sociological research on human behaviour in online spaces and other computer-mediated systems. The method depends on the research question, suitable data access, and ethical safeguards.

methods.name: computational modelling of neural activity and brain systems
methods.description: Build and interpret computational models of neural activity and brain processes, from cells and circuits to systems and behaviour. This is a research specialization, not a requirement for every neuroscience or cognitive-science role.
